full_judgment:
2. The appellant as plaintiff filed a suit for partition of the schedule property stating, inter alia, that Mangia Sk. had 6 annas 8 pies share in C.S. Khatian No. 264 and 269 described in Schedule Ka and Kha respectively and that he had 8 annas share in C.S. Khatian No. 267 and 271, the properties in Schedule "Ga" and "Gha" thereby claiming 2.34 acres of land to their share. 

 7. The bone of contention is whether the property belonged to Uli Fakir entirely or whether Mangai Fakir had 8 annas share in C.S. Khatian Nos. 261 and 271 as alleged by the plaintiff. Admittedly Uli Fakir left behind two sons Mangai Sk. and Bocha Sk. and two daughters Kulsum and Alimunnessa; so by law of Inheritance Mangai inherited 5 annas four pies i.e. one third share in the suit property. The finding of fact that the total quantum of suit property is 12.77 acres and consequently Mangai having inherited one-third share inherited 4.26 acres. The next admitted position is that Mangai transferred 2.25 acres and therefore he was Left with only 2.01 acres. This was found by the appellate Court below. The appellate Court below pointed out that the defendants in paragraph 5 of the written statement challenged the contention of the plaintiff that be had 8 annas share in C.S. 267 and 271. It was asserted that Uli Fakir was the owner of this property. 

 14. Mr. B.N. Chowdhury cited Farok Ahmed Meah and others versus Lalit Mohan Chowdhury and others, AIR. 1939 Calcutta 582 where it was held that when the respondent has made it clear that he wanted to maintain the decree of the lower court and did not want it to be disturbed, he without preferring any appeal or filing a Memorandum of Cross-objection cannot challenge a finding the result of which would be to destroy in effect the foundation on which the part decree was made in favour of the appellant by the lower court rests. This case has no manner of application inasmuch as the defendants in this case at the earliest opportunity challenged the contention of the plaintiff that he was the owner to the extent of 8 minas share in the respective Khatian and their version was that it was an ejmali property belonging to Uli Fakir the common ancestor of the plaintiff. The plaintiff, on perusal of the written statement attempted to amend the plaint but no evidence was given by them to substantiate their contention that this property was not ejmali property.
